subject: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex — great to meet you and Samir on the call earlier. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can size the right proposal: 

Summary of what you shared:
- Expected monthly token consumption (dev -> prod ramp): ~80M–150M tokens/month initially, target 6–12 months out.
- Peak/burst behavior: short bursts up to ~3k RPS for 1–3 minutes during promotions.
- Target unit economics: looking for a target $/1M tokens in the $30–$45 range (goal is <$40 if possible).
- Budget range: rough target $8k–$12k/month for this phase.

Questions we still need to confirm (can you please reply inline):
1) Exact monthly tokens for the pilot (Mar–May). If you have a ballpark: dev 10–20M, pilot 50–80M, prod 120–200M?
2) Typical prompt/response length (avg tokens per call) and ratio of embedding vs generation usage.
3) Any compliance constraints (data residency/SOC2) that would affect routing or private deployment?

Proposal options we discussed (high level):
A) On-demand + burst buffer (no commit): on-demand unit = $60 / 1M tokens; burst buffer allows 2x quota for short bursts (first 72 hours at up to 2x, then overage applies).
B) Committed reserved capacity (3–12 month): discounted unit economics, example $20–$30 / 1M tokens depending on commit. This includes an agreed baseline quota and lower overage rates.
C) Short-term pilot addendum: temporary quota increase for the pilot period with a blended unit rate.

Attachments: I attached a short rate limits & overage overview and a draft addendum to illustrate the pilot path.

Next steps I can take this week:
- Draft a short pilot addendum with a requested quota increase (needs signing)
- Put in a temporary burst quota in our system for one week so you can run the traffic pattern you described
- Share an itemized estimate for the pilot (breakdown by reserved vs on-demand)

If that sounds right, please confirm the pilot token estimate and whether you want us to enable the temporary quota increase while we finalize terms.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

----
Attachment: rate_limits_overview_v1.pdf (1 page)
Attachment: draft_addendum_acme.docx (1 file)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap. Confirming inline: 

1) Pilot token estimate: plan is ~50M tokens for a 30-day pilot. Prod target after successful pilot: ~120M tokens/month.
2) Average generation: ~200 tokens in prompt + ~250 tokens generated (so ~450 tokens per call on average). Embeddings usage is currently minimal (<5% of calls).
3) Compliance: SOC2 Type II in progress; we need evidence of audit logs and data retention controls — but routing to US regions is fine today.

On budget/unit economics: our procurement team has a firm target of ~$35 / 1M tokens as the ceiling for the pilot. If on-demand is $60 that’s out of range; we are therefore evaluating a short reserved commitment or a blended pilot rate.

Regarding bursts: our traffic will have spikes (3k RPS) for ~2–3 minutes during certain workflows. Important to understand any hard throttles vs soft limits and whether you can guarantee short burst allowance without failed requests. Also curious about invoice cadence and how overage is billed (monthly, pro-rated).

Please go ahead and: 
- Enable a temporary quota increase for the 30-day pilot (we want to exercise burst patterns).
- Send the pilot addendum with the blended rate so procurement can get eyes on it.
- Include a sample invoice example that shows how on-demand vs reserved overages would appear.

Thanks —
Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com
+1 (212) 555-0147

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Alex — great, that helps a lot. Actions we just did and what we propose next: 

What I enabled now:
- Temporary pilot quota: +2x baseline for 30 days (active immediately) so you can validate burst patterns. This is a soft buffer — we will not hard-throttle within that allowance; requests above the buffer will be metered as overage.

Pilot commercial options (pick one):
1) Blended pilot addendum (recommended): 30-day pilot at $38 / 1M tokens with the temporary quota enabled. If you convert to a 6-month reserved commit within 30 days, we will apply a $7 / 1M credit retroactively to tokens consumed during the pilot.
2) Short reserved commitment (3 months): baseline 120M tokens/month commit at $28 / 1M tokens; overage at $45 / 1M.
3) On-demand only (not recommended for your target economics): $60 / 1M tokens; burst buffer subject to availability.

Overage billing & terms:
- Billing cadence: monthly invoice; overages billed on the following month with line-item token usage and rate (example invoice attached).
- Burst allowance: temporary buffer we enabled covers short spikes; after buffer is consumed, overages apply at the overage rate tied to the chosen commercial path.
- Quota increase process: we can escalate permanent quota increases within 48 hours once procurement signs the addendum.

Next steps I will take today:
- Send the DocuSign link for the pilot addendum (if you pick the blended pilot option).
- Share an itemized estimate and a sample invoice for your finance team.
- Loop Rafael (engineering solutions) to confirm that there are no hard throttles and that error modes return 429 with X-Quota headers for graceful handling.

Camila and Rafael — can you confirm the short-term buffer configuration and the example invoice PDF? Rafael, if you can add one sentence on whether 3k RPS bursts for 2–3 minutes is a normal pattern or if we should recommend different buffering, that would be great.

Alex — if you confirm you want the blended pilot at $38 / 1M tokens I’ll send the DocuSign now.

Best,
Marissa

----
Attachment: rate_limits_overview_v1.pdf (updated)
Attachment: sample_invoice_example.pdf

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Rate limits & overage pricing — follow-up and next steps

Marissa — thanks, that all looks good. We’ll go with the blended pilot at $38 / 1M tokens. Please send the DocuSign and the itemized estimate so procurement can route it. Also please confirm the pilot quota is live (we’re going to start load tests this afternoon).

One last ask from procurement: can you add a 30-day termination clause to the pilot addendum? They want the ability to cancel if the pilot materially exceeds budget or fails certain SLOs.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex
